slots.anchor: This book kept forgetting how to write itself.
slots.brief: Margin vignette: an open manuscript whose ink is lifting off the page like steam from the earlier chapters while a hand rewrites the same marginal correction again; a faint ghost of the same correction visible twice before. Melancholy, wry.

slots.anchor: Knowledge engineering is back. It is carrying Markdown.
slots.brief: Small spot: a 1980s expert-systems consultant's leather briefcase, reopened; instead of logic rules it spills plain paper notes with hash-mark headings (illegible squiggles, not readable text). One robot peers in, delighted.

Corner scene: a small hillside town where each building visibly answers a recurring situation — a shaded corner where two paths meet, a window seat catching afternoon light, a market arcade — with faint pencil construction lines still showing, as if the town remembers why each form exists.

slots.anchor: ## Popper: A Pattern Needs a Way to Lose
slots.brief: Margin vignette: a pattern written on a workshop card, hung on a nail — and beside it a small hammer on a cord, provided for breaking it. The card has a designated strike zone. No readable text; the affordance carries the idea.

slots.anchor: ## Feyerabend: The Librarian Is Also a Hypothesis
slots.text: Bad storage forgets by deletion. Bad retrieval forgets by attention.

slots.anchor: The librarian is no longer merely finding books.
slots.brief: Margin vignette: a robot librarian rolling a ladder along shelves — but the shelves themselves are subtly curving to funnel toward one favored alcove, worn floorboards showing the path everyone was steered down. Quietly sinister.
